summary: Psalm 117 calls every nation and every people to praise Yahweh. It grounds that worldwide summons in Yahweh’s loving kindness, which is great toward “us,” and his faithfulness, which endures forever.
whyItMatters: This shortest psalm stands in Book V of Psalms, where the collection moves toward broad and repeated praise. Its two verses turn Israel’s praise outward, inviting all peoples to join in honoring Yahweh’s enduring kindness and faithfulness.

context.author: Psalms is an anthology with many writers and collections; Psalm 117 names no individual author in the text.
context.audience: Israel’s worshiping and instructed community, with later Jewish and Christian communities also adopting the Psalms for prayer and worship.
context.date: Individual psalms may preserve material from the monarchy through the postexilic period; assigning one date to the whole Psalter would be misleading.
context.setting: Book V of the Psalter, among poems shaped for praise, thanksgiving, Torah reflection, pilgrimage, and the final movement toward Hallelujah.
context.literaryForm: Very compressed Hebrew poetry and communal praise, built from a summons in verse 1 and the reason for praise in verse 2.

outline.heading: Summons to all peoples
outline.note: The psalm commands all nations and peoples to praise and extol Yahweh.

outline.heading: Reason and closing praise
outline.note: The psalm grounds that summons in Yahweh’s great loving kindness and enduring faithfulness, then closes with “Praise Yah!”

keyVerses.text: Praise Yahweh, all you nations! Extol him, all you peoples!
keyVerses.why: This is the psalm’s opening movement: praise is not addressed only to one group but summoned from all nations and peoples.

keyVerses.text: For his loving kindness is great toward us. Yahweh’s faithfulness endures forever. Praise Yah!
keyVerses.why: This verse gives the reason for praise and names the two divine qualities the psalm emphasizes: loving kindness and faithfulness.

questions.question: Why is this chapter so short?
questions.answer: The psalm has only two verses, and the psalm does not develop a story or argument at length. Its force comes from compression: a universal call to praise in verse 1 and the reason for that praise in verse 2.

questions.question: Who is being told to praise Yahweh?
questions.answer: Verse 1 addresses “all you nations” and “all you peoples.” The wording makes the summons wider than Israel alone, though the reason in verse 2 is spoken from an “us” perspective.

questions.question: What does “Extol” mean here?
questions.answer: In verse 1, “Extol him” stands beside “Praise Yahweh.” In plain terms, it means to honor or lift up Yahweh in praise; the second line reinforces the first rather than introducing a separate action.

questions.question: Who is “us” in “toward us”?
questions.answer: The verse does not identify the speaker beyond the worshiping voice of the psalm. In the setting of Psalms, the “us” naturally sounds like the community using the psalm, but the chapter itself does not name a specific occasion or group more precisely.

questions.question: What reason does the psalm give for worldwide praise?
questions.answer: Verse 2 gives two reasons: Yahweh’s loving kindness is great toward “us,” and Yahweh’s faithfulness endures forever. The psalm does not list specific events; it praises God’s enduring character in broad terms.

questions.question: Does the chapter say the nations have already joined the praise?
questions.answer: No. Verse 1 is a command or invitation: “Praise” and “Extol.” The chapter summons all nations and peoples; it does not narrate their response.

questions.question: What is the difference between “loving kindness” and “faithfulness” in this verse?
questions.answer: The psalm places both terms side by side as reasons to praise Yahweh. “Loving kindness” points to gracious commitment, while “faithfulness” points to reliability that “endures forever”; the chapter emphasizes both without explaining them further.

questions.question: Why does the psalm end with “Praise Yah!” after already calling for praise?
questions.answer: The ending returns to the psalm’s main action. After giving the reason for praise, the final words renew the command in a brief closing burst.

glossary.def: The main action commanded in the psalm: honoring Yahweh with worshipful speech.
The divine name used in this World English Bible translation.
The peoples beyond one local group who are included in the psalm’s call to praise.
The quality named in verse 2 as great toward “us,” giving a reason for praise.
The quality named in verse 2 as enduring forever.
